subject: Acme procurement: PO restriction and exception request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lennox <sara.lennox@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme procurement: PO restriction and exception request

Hi Sara,

Great to speak this morning — thanks for walking me through Acme's plans for the internal search + assistant pilot. Per our call, two commercial/ops items to confirm so we can get the pilot started next week:

1) Payment path: you mentioned your procurement team does not allow vendor-issued invoices tied to long-term net-30-style POs for new SaaS vendors under $50k MRR, and they prefer marketplace or credit-card prepay for pilots. Can you confirm whether Acme can accept AWS Marketplace billing, or whether we need a signed exception to proceed?

2) Contracting: I attached a one-page SOW and the standard Redwood order form. If procurement requires a PO number on the order form, please share the exact PO workflow (PO issuance timeline and approver).

If the PO path is blocked, we can proceed with a short prepaid card agreement for the pilot (30 days) or request a procurement exception. For the latter, I can pull in our sales ops and legal to get you the right paperwork quickly.

Next steps I propose: you confirm whether marketplace billing is an option by EOD Tues; if not, let me know procurement's acceptable exception language and any internal spend thresholds. I'll follow up with Marissa (cc'd) to initiate an exception request if needed.

Thanks — excited to get you running.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_Draft.docx

From: Sara Lennox <sara.lennox@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme procurement: PO restriction and exception request

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the recap — summarized correctly. Quick answers:

- We cannot route new SaaS vendors through AWS Marketplace for this kind of internal pilot due to our cloud vendor policy; Marketplace is only for production SaaS purchases.
- Our procurement policy requires a PO for any vendor engagement, but procurement leadership has signoff authority only for contracts > $25k/year. For pilots below that, we typically pay on card or use a short-term prepaid invoice.
- We do have a blanket policy that prohibits paying without a PO if the vendor insists on invoice billing tied to a contract (no-exception), however, exceptions can be made by procurement leadership in special cases (security/compliance approved vendors).

For this pilot (anticipated ~$8k), procurement prefers card payment. However, our internal finance team requires a vendor risk review and vendor registration before we can put the card on file. I'll loop in procurement to confirm the vendor registration ETA (usually 3-5 business days).

If you can accept card prepay for the pilot, that will be the smoothest path. Otherwise, we'll need a procurement exception and leadership approval, which will take longer.

Best,
Sara
Sara Lennox
Senior Program Manager, Search Platform
Acme Corporation

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lennox <sara.lennox@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme procurement: PO restriction and exception request

Thanks Sara — that helps.

We can absolutely take card prepay for an $8k pilot. Two quick asks so we can get payment and the pilot scheduled:

- Can procurement provide the vendor registration checklist or a link so we can submit our company details today?
- If vendor registration will take longer than 3 business days, would procurement consider a one-time exception to allow invoice billing with a PO for the pilot only? That would require procurement leadership signoff; if helpful I can supply a short vendor profile and security artifacts (SOC 2 Type II, data flow diagram).

Marissa / Rishi — looping you both in to advise on the fastest internal path. If we need a formal exception, can Sales Ops help prepare the exception request and attach the security docs? I can draft the ask and provide the SOW and PO language.

Ben

From: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Lennox <sara.lennox@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme procurement: PO restriction and exception request

Ben / Sara,

Procurement — quick note on timing. Vendor registration for Redwood will require the following documents: W-9, SOC 2 report (or equivalent), bank remittance info, and a completed vendor questionnaire. Estimated time to onboard once we have complete docs: 5-7 business days.

For pilot spend <$10k, standard practice is to pay on card; procurement can approve a one-time exception to invoice billing only if the vendor is already in our vendor registry. We do not issue POs to cover pre-contract pilot engagements unless the vendor is on our registry.

If Redwood can accept card and provide the vendor questionnaire now, we can start the onboarding right away. If Redwood cannot accept card, please submit an exception request form and note that procurement leadership may require CFO approval because this would be a deviation from the vendor-first policy.

Regards,
Acme Procurement
procurement@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Thanks for the context — looping in Sales Ops and Legal to expedite. Rishi, can you confirm we have an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II and W-9 in the shared folder? I'll draft a short exception request packet if Acme needs leadership signoff (include risk summary, pilot value, and proposed controls for data handling).

Ben — I'll prepare the vendor questionnaire response and the minimum security artifacts today. If Acme can accept card prepay, we'll provide a payment link + vendor questionnaire ASAP so they can start onboarding within 24 hours. If procurement insists on an invoice with PO, we'll prepare the exception form; note that CFO approval could add 7-10 business days.

I'll attach the vendor profile and exception template to the HubSpot deal and send you the DocuSign link for the SOW once the payment path is decided.

Marissa Cole
